transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I came in because I keep avoiding my own workshop, and family get-togethers if my brother-in-law might be there. I’m tired of planning my life around not running into those reminders.
Did something traumatic happen involving your brother-in-law or your workshop?
It’s tied to both, yes. I keep clear of the workshop, and I avoid family gatherings if my brother-in-law will be there. I’m tired of having to arrange everything around those reminders.
Did your brother-in-law or something in the workshop involve an event where you were seriously harmed or thought you might be?
I’m not sure I want to get into the details right now. It’s difficult to talk about.
At the time of what happened, did you believe that you or someone else might be killed or seriously injured?
I… I’m not ready to say exactly what I believed at the time. It’s hard to go back to that.
Do unwanted memories of what happened ever suddenly come into your mind?
Yes. Out of nowhere, I’ll see his hand with that heavy tool again—like a picture popping into my head when I’m shaving or working on a painting. My chest still tightens when it happens.
Do you have nightmares about what happened?
Yes, sometimes. I wake up from a bad dream about the workshop, and then I’m wide awake for an hour or two. Other nights I just lie there listening for noises in the house.
Are you jumpy or constantly on guard, even when there isn’t any real danger?
Yes. Even at the senior center or down at the church basement, I catch myself looking over who’s come in, where the door is, and whether somebody’s standing too close behind me.
Do you try to push away thoughts or feelings about what happened?
Yes. I avoid my workshop, and I skip family get-togethers if there’s a chance my brother-in-law will be there. I’m tired of having to plan everything around not running into those reminders.
When something reminds you of what happened, does your body react strongly, like your heart racing or feeling suddenly tense?
Yes. It can happen out of nowhere—I’ll see his hand holding that heavy tool again, like a picture in my head when I’m shaving or working on a painting. My chest tightens right up when it does.
Do you feel this fear and avoidance mainly because it reminds you of what happened in the workshop?
Yes, mostly. I keep away from my workshop, and I avoid family gatherings if I think my brother-in-law might be there. I’m tired of arranging my life around those reminders.
Do you ever feel as if the event is happening again, not just that you remember it?
No, I don’t think it feels like it’s happening again. It’s more that the memory comes up and makes me tense.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling down most days.
When you avoid family gatherings, is it because you’re afraid of seeing your brother-in-law and being reminded of what happened?
Yes. If I think he might be there, I’d rather not go. Seeing him brings it all back, so I avoid the gathering—and my workshop too. I’m tired of having to plan around it.
Have these symptoms been going on for more than a month?
Yes. It’s been going on since the confrontation with my brother-in-law, about two years and four months now.
